name: Center for Global Development (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults by branch: the pneumococcal AMC 80% (children in the 60 Gavi countries that introduced PCV, weighted roughly by births: India, Nigeria, Pakistan, Ethiopia, DR Congo, Bangladesh, then smaller East and West African countries and Afghanistan), the development banks' extra lending 17% (their largest borrowers: India, Indonesia, Turkey, Egypt, Brazil, the Philippines, Ukraine, Nigeria, Kenya, Bangladesh), MCC 3% (its African compact countries). A judgment: no country split of the credited value is published.
summary: The Center for Global Development, a Washington think tank with a London arm (US$23.9 million spent in 2025), researches and argues for better aid and development policy. An average year of its spending since 2002 (about 80% of 2025's in real terms) is counted against its credited share of three wins: the advance market commitment for pneumococcal vaccines its working group designed (a judged 40% of PCV's faster spread to 60 poor countries, about 180,000 child deaths a year averted at scale, with the children's later income and GiveWell's shared supplements, net of what Gavi and the countries' health budgets would otherwise have done with the money, times CGD's 15% of the effort), the development banks' 2022-2025 capital reforms (5% of US$200 billion of extra lending, valued at a loan's grant element as aid) and the Millennium Challenge Corporation's design (10% of a judged 10% improvement in its US$1.2 billion a year of compacts, in 2025 prices), each counted for the years a won reform counts, with its other work (3ie, migration, debt relief) at a judged 40% more. With the next dollar at {{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} of the average, it comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per 1,000 dollars, mostly because the vaccine branch counts deaths averted across a programme that reached 33 million children a year, of which a small credited share still outweighs a budget of about US$20 million a year. The result is mostly uncertainty: CGD's share of the credit, the AMC's share of the acceleration and the years a win counts are judgments with no study behind them; all three branches are discounted by the shared missing-data slider.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: MCC: value of the compacts signed since its creation (US$)

source.title: Congressional Research Service, Millennium Challenge Corporation (IF12850), updated 10 September 2026
source.quote: Since its creation, MCC has signed 50 compacts in 33 countries worth over $18 billion.

rows.explainer: Compacts are MCC's main programmes. 'Over US$18 billion' is what was signed, before terminations (CRS Table 2 lists four ongoing compacts terminated in 2025, and some earlier ones were cut short), so the money spent is lower: US$18.5 billion (16 to 20 billion), in the nominal dollars of the years signed.

rows.explainer: The compacts signed since 2005 over the years of signing, in 2025 prices from those of 2015, the middle year of signing (Convention 8): about US$1.2 billion a year.

rows.label: AMC: under-five deaths averted by PCV in Gavi countries through 2015

source.title: Gavi, Pneumococcal AMC outcomes and impact evaluation (Boston Consulting Group, 2015)
source.quote: an estimated 230,000 to 290,000 under-five deaths averted, with over 3 million projected by 2030

rows.explainer: The evaluation's modelled estimate for the first cohorts; it projects over 3 million by 2030, which our yearly figure below matches (about 180,000 a year).

rows.label: AMC: under-five deaths averted per child fully immunised
rows.explainer: The evaluation's deaths through 2015 over the children immunised through 2014.

rows.label: Value of an under-five death averted, units of value
rows.explainer: The site's value of a death under five (GiveWell's moral weight) times the life-value multiplier.

rows.label: AMC: doses of PCV per child fully immunised

source.title: Gavi, Pneumococcal AMC outcomes and impact evaluation (Boston Consulting Group, 2015)
source.quote: fully immunised with three PCV doses

rows.explainer: Three doses, as the evaluation counts full immunisation.

rows.label: AMC: price per dose under the AMC (US$)

source.title: Gavi, Pneumococcal vaccine support
source.note: Also on the page: the AMC price of no more than US$ 3.50 per dose, and a third manufacturer's US$ 2.00 per dose.

rows.explainer: The AMC capped the long-term price at US$3.50; by early 2019 a supplier's lowest offer was US$2.90 and a third maker offered US$2.00 from 2020, so most 2015-2019 doses cost less than the cap: US$3.00 (2.00 to 3.50).

rows.label: AMC: cost of delivering a dose in routine immunisation (US$)
rows.explainer: Adding a vaccine to an existing schedule costs cold chain, staff time and waste beyond the dose price. Judged US$1 a dose (0.5 to 2.5), anchored on the incremental delivery costs of new vaccines in low-income countries' routine programmes (about a dollar a dose in costing studies of PCV and rotavirus introductions).

rows.label: AMC: donors' commitment to the pneumococcal AMC (US$)

source.title: Gavi, Pneumococcal AMC outcomes and impact evaluation (Boston Consulting Group, 2015)

rows.explainer: Paid as a top-up on the first doses bought; spread below over all children reached by 2019 so the cost per child includes it.

rows.label: AMC: vaccine money per child immunised (US$)
rows.explainer: Three doses at the price paid, plus the donors' AMC top-up spread over the children reached by 2019. Paid by Gavi, its donors and the countries' co-financing, never by CGD.

rows.label: AMC: delivery cost per child immunised (US$)
rows.explainer: Three doses' delivery, paid by the countries' health systems.

rows.label: AMC: what the money spent per child would otherwise have done, units of value
rows.explainer: Its use is known (normalization.md 2.20): the vaccine money is Gavi's and its donors', valued at GiveWell's figure for a dollar of Gavi spending (@givewell_shared.cf_value_gavi), what Gavi would otherwise have bought; the delivery is the countries' own health spending, at GiveWell's figure for domestic government spending (@givewell_shared.cf_value_government).

rows.label: Value of a dollar of aid whose use isn't known, units of value
rows.explainer: The shared value of a donor's aid budget dollar (@aid_value.oda_vs_cash, about 1 times cash, 0.4 to 2) times cash's value (normalization.md 2.20): what the money the banks lend or MCC spends would otherwise have done (both of unknown use: every sector).

rows.label: AMC: later-income gain of the children protected, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: Children spared pneumococcal disease earn more as adults: GiveWell's shared ratio of the income gain to the value of deaths averted, re-based to the site's discount rate, value of income (a doubling is ln 2 of ln-consumption, @givewell_shared.ln_consumption_per_doubling) and value of a life.

rows.label: AMC: value of a year of PCV in Gavi countries net of its cost, units of value
rows.explainer: Children reached a year times the deaths averted per child at the value of a death, with the later-income gain, and GiveWell's supplementary shares (illness, treatment costs, investment of income, herd protection, serotype replacement) on the deaths' and income's value together, as in the direct-health chain, less what the money spent would otherwise have done.

rows.label: MDB capital reforms: value of a dollar lent, as a share of a dollar of aid
rows.explainer: A loan is repaid, so a dollar lent is worth less than a dollar given: its grant element (the saving against what the borrower would otherwise pay, or the projects it couldn't finance at all). The extra lending is mostly the banks' non-concessional windows, whose grant element against borrowers' market rates is about 10-20% (OECD's grant-equivalent method at 6-7% discount rates). Judged 15% (5% to 40%; the high end for countries with no market access).

rows.label: MDB capital reforms: share of the extra capacity actually lent
rows.explainer: Headroom is a capacity; banks lend it only as projects and borrowers' demand allow, and some was kept as a buffer for ratings. Judged 60% (30% to 90%).

rows.label: MDB capital reforms: value of a year's extra lending, units of value
rows.explainer: Extra lending a year, the share lent, its value per dollar against aid, and aid's value.

rows.label: MCC: how much more a dollar of MCC's aid does than a dollar of other aid
rows.explainer: CGD's design proposals (selecting countries by published indicators, country-led compacts, a 10% economic-return hurdle, independent evaluations) aimed to make MCC's dollars do more than other US aid. Its evaluations find mixed income effects and its own economic returns often below plan. Judged 10% better (0 to 30%), anchored on the gap cash-benchmarking finds between better and typical aid programmes (@aid_value.oda_vs_cash's note).

rows.label: MCC: value of a year's improvement in its aid, units of value
rows.explainer: MCC's yearly funding times aid's value, times the improvement in its own aid plus the reforms countries make to qualify (a side effect, as a share of MCC's whole value).

rows.label: Chance the policy change happens
rows.explainer: All three wins happened (the AMC from 2009, MCC from 2004, the banks' reforms from 2022): 1.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (Your values → How impact is counted; docs/normalization.md 2.9). Never the charity's or an evaluator's own years.

rows.label: AMC: years from CGD's work (2003-2005) to PCV at scale
rows.explainer: The working group reported in 2005; the AMC launched in 2007, the first doses came in 2010 and the yearly reach counted is 2015-2019's. Judged 7 years (5 to 10).

rows.label: MDB capital reforms: years from CGD's work (2021-2023) to the extra lending
